1559584696793567232.report: Just as the title says. Rank 10 BST pet still summoning at lvl 49 and not 50. Necromancer and Mage pets are being summoned at lvl 50, though. BST pet is Rank 10, Nec and Mage pets are Rank 8 with focus item.

replies.text: That is the max level of a Beast pet with +10 The intial warder is level 39, +10 is 49. Without a focus, that'll be the cap of the warder. Not a bug

replies.text: Just tested without focus, and Rank 8 Mage pet, and bumped Necro pet to 10. Both are summoning at lvl 50. Seems like a bug to me.

replies.text: It's not a bug, 39 is the level of the Warder pet. Add 10 to that. It's 49. Unless you can mote the spell to +11, or find a BST pet focus that doesn't exist right now, 49 is the max level of the BST pet

replies.author: vorpaldicepress
replies.text: The warder was never capped at 49 because of the Player Level-1 cap before, it was capped at 49 (and still is) because that's the highest it can get with moting.

replies.author: Cica
replies.text: I'm seeing what you're writing, and I understand it. Not arguing that. That is how it WAS before todays patch. I have tested Mage, Necro, Enchanter, and Beastlord pets. I have everything at lvl 50, and all pets are at least lvl 7. Directly from the patch notes: *Increased the level cap for upgraded player pets from player level - 1 to player level. * Now, that being said, this is a bug. They made it so that the pets scale up with the motes, as they never had before Enhanced Minion items existed for pet classes besides the traditional necro book and mage items. I am aware that BST doesn't have anything in this vein. BST didn't get introduced until Luclin, so everything for them was retconned. The language is very plain. So are the impacts of this bug. No pet was ever able to be upgraded like this, so that goes to state that there will be bugs. Just like the grow bugs that exist with BST pets specifically right now. I have also posted about this. Necro Pet Rank 10 (no focus) = Lvl 50 Necro Pet Rank 10 (with focus) = Lvl 50 (some stat increases) Mage Pet Rank 8 (no focus) = Lvl 50 Mage Pet Rank 8 (with focus) = Lvl 50 Bst Pet Rank 10 = Lvl 49

replies.author: Soulspurn
replies.text: You've very clearly either misunderstood what was said, contrary to your claim otherwise, or don't understand that there are TWO limits on pet level. One based off pet spell level (max is up to +10 max level for any pet) and the other, which USED TO cap pet levels at 49, even if spell level or focus would push it higher. They only updated the second , so spell levels/focii can get them to 50. But that only applies it the spell level+focii would push it that high. If BST pet starts at 39, you're not getting it to 50.

replies.text: Your buff is working as intended and the proc is maxed at V, you're good to go and its working as intended.

replies.author: Nakar
replies.text: This seems to happen anywhere with purely underwater mobs. For instance, it will happen in Runnyeye. It's probably related to something about how fish and other aquatic enemies want to path to the player but can't, but also something about them being aquatic prevents them from eventually losing the player like random lv8 skeletons will in land zones.

replies.author: Nakar
replies.text: There's probably some routine that blocks them going out of the water and then maybe skipping whatever it is eventually breaks combat.

replies.author: Nakar
replies.text: Notice that if you aggro another island in Sky they eventually give up -- but everything in Sky is a land mob.

replies.author: Nakar
replies.text: I'm not sure how fixable this is because it sounds like ancient EQ jank, but it'd be interesting if they could figure it out.

replies.author: Nakar
replies.text: Basically my hypothesis if they ever look into this: Probably, there's a routine in the aggro code where the mob asks, "Can I path to the player?", and if the answer is no, it breaks combat. But for fish, there's another check that asks, "Can I leave the water to path to the player?", and if the answer is no, they don't leave. My guess is that "Can I path to the player?" is treated as yes for fish -- because a regular mob could just leave the water and path to your location -- even though "Can I leave the water to path to the player?" is no.

replies.author: Nakar
replies.text: So they sit there not pathing but staying aggroed.

replies.author: Nakar
replies.text: The OG devs probably noticed fish coming out of the water to chase people and realized that was silly and put in something to keep them from doing that but didn't completely replicate the combat drop part.

replies.author: Nakar
replies.text: Could be worth trying to address this because mobs constantly calculating useless pathing they're not going to utilize might be a (probably small) performance hit.

replies.author: stars2heaven
replies.text: why would you be stuck with no mana going into fear because of a fish not dropping agro?

replies.author: Nakar
replies.text: Presumably they ritual to Feerrott, get fish aggro before their mana regens sufficiently, get to the Fear portal and Voidling area with the fish still aggro'd. I wouldn't say that's the worst place for it -- as I mentioned, it happens in lower Runnyeye and can be a huge pain there -- but it is conceivable why it would be irritating.

replies.author: Nakar
replies.text: It is a legitimate targeting/aggro bug, but I'm just not sure how much GJ can do about it if it's been in the game forever.

replies.author: Nakar
replies.text: Stuff that can't path to you is supposed to give up. Some things that can't path to you don't ever give up. That's a legitimate bug.

replies.author: Gorthaur
replies.text: I figured out what is happening... Its the scroll options window, when you right click on book, and slelect load, save or delete... Even if you physically click save, so it is highlighted in red, and the sub menu opens, when you mouse over the sub menu... Because the submenu necessarrily opens lower than the previous menu choice, if your cursor deviates from the edge of the sub menu panel at all, even with Save physically selected and locked red, the panel shifts lower and becomes the mneu for the delete option, rather than save. So when you are looking at it, you see save highlighted in red, you see the submenu open, but it is actually the sub menu for the delete option. You believe, based on what you are seeing; that you are saving, when in fact you are deleting. Need to modify the panels so that when a top option like Save is selected in RED, it locks the subpanel to that option, and doesn't allow it to float to other options.

1545871155725074524.title: Lull Randomly Dropping from NPCs
1545871155725074524.report:
I haven’t nailed down specific circumstances that are causing this to happen but lately I’ve noticed all of the calm/lull spells/songs seem to randomly drop on NPCs they are used on. 

This isn’t logged as far as I can tell (ie. no messages that it drops due to duration expiring) and I’m not seeing the NPC casting anything to dispel or otherwise remove it.

A recent example was last night in the undead castle area of the Hole. Playing PAL/SHM/NEC, I used both the highest level Paladin lull as well as the necro version on a ghost and watched the debuff icon show up and then disappear within 1-2 seconds of it landing on one of the ghost NPCs. The NPC was not aggroed, not a named or rare spawn and I didn’t see it or other NPCs in the room casting anything to remove it.

I’ve observed this indirectly as well when I’ve lulled several NPCs (seeing it land on each before moving on to next) and then noticing a few of the NPCs I just successfully lulled losing it well before the duration is due to expire. 

At first I thought I was just losing my mind and not getting lull on all of the NPCs in the room but after I had unintentional aggro a few times I started paying more attention and noticed the debuff icon dropping within seconds of it successfully applying. 

I’m not aware of any normal game mechanics that would cause this to happen unless there’s a “cleanup” routine running to remove debuffs when an NPC is not in combat (similar to how DoTs and other debuffs drop from players when out of combat). In which case I would expect lull abilities to be excluded since they’re meant to be used out of combat.

replies.author: jakken
replies.text: i believe pacify spells have always had a chance to fade early, i always get a message that its worn off when it happens. its like root or charm, not like mez. found this info with a quick google: Lull fails work like this: When a lull spell lands on a NPC, the NPC's MR is ignored and instead 15 MR is used. The 15 MR is still modified by level difference, meaning mobs 6 levels and under below the caster will never aggro. If the spell resists, then a second roll is done using the caster's charisma. This roll is: 90 - CHA / 4. Failing this roll results in a critical fail and the NPC aggroing on the caster; otherwise the NPC will ignore the resist. If there is a cap to the charisma critical failure chance, then it's not seemingly hit at 305 CHA. I did not parse beyond 305. Lulls have a chance to fade early. The precise logic is unknown, however parses resulted in this: 7% per tick on a +5 a red con 2% per tick on white cons 1% per tick on a -1 blue. 0% per tick on a -5 blue

1545117591209775165.title: Grandmaster R'Tal in POHate with visible Sunderfury equipped won't slow below the wpn haste normal?
1545117591209775165.report:
In regular EQ if a mob has a piece of gear displayed (weapon etc) then it drops that weapon. In EQL a mob can have a weapon displayed but it is "phantom" and may or may not drop. Today I slowed Grandmaster R'Tal who had a visible Sunderfury which has a worn haste effect. When I slowed him it did not slow the weaopn haste and I had pillaged all his other buffs (D4 mob). When he died there was no Sunderfury. 

Is it normal that a slow does not affect worn haste of a mob? And if it is not normal, would the fact that the Sunderfury was a "phantom" and not real weapon make it immune to the effects of slow? Not sure if this is a bug or if I am ignorant of this particular mechanic thanks in advance.

replies.author: Tubasnot
replies.text: Weapon display I know are mostly just “oh it can happen to spawn it it like normal”. But the drop from mobs is totally separate as it’s generated after the mob dies for the individual player(s). As far as the slow, I am not sure. My understanding of slow what that it overwrites all haste (spell + worn). I.e. you got a haste buff for 30% and a worn of 30% making your attack speed 160 Then you get slowed by a spell that lows by 35%. It would negate your haste and then slow you, setting attack speed at 65 Where 100 being default normal haste. Hope this helps and anyone feel free correct me if I’m in the wrong here.

replies.author: feltz916
replies.text: Weapon display is what they actually have equipped, so the OP is likely correct and its giving weapon haste. Drop table gets randomized on kill now rather than spawn. I'm curious how you tested this, just my watching him not slow down?

replies.author: dxmachina2429
replies.text: Yes I farm R'Tal 3 or 4 times daily to upgrade my warrior and the Sunderfury is a rare drop. When I did the typical debuffs I was surprised at his attack speed which was higher than normal. I pillage and slow/malo/cripple and can kill this guy in my sleep having done it so many times.

replies.author: feltz916
replies.text: im sure its working just fine. Slow is not intended to remove haste, just oppose it

replies.author: dxmachina2429
replies.text: Pretty sure he was at full weapon haste and my slow should have mitigated it substantially. I suspect that worn haste of npcs is not being affected at all by player slow debuffs

replies.author: oSlash
replies.text: Would be good to log and parse your fights the next time you see him with the weapon equipped. That's the only way to be sure that he's attacking faster than base. Attacking faster than normal slowed speed is expected. Just like players can now attack faster when slowed as slow doesn't negate just opposes haste.

replies.author: Standing
replies.text: Recent patch made haste/slow effects stack instead of slow completely making haste irrelevant. So he could be at 136% or 140% not sure if weapons scale up on mobs then depending on strength of slow could still be above 100%.

replies.author: Standing
replies.text: Disarm would probably remove the haste.

replies.author: Kreigr
replies.text: Casting w/in 1 to 2s of the end of being stunned seems to always cause the spell be interrupted

replies.author: Viskar
replies.text: To add more info, the server seems to calculate a separate pushback amount for stuns that is separate from the client-side stun pushback, causing a position desync that doesn't get resolved until the stun ends. While stunned the client's actual position is ignored by the server, so when the stun ends the client finally tells the server where it is. But if this happens while casting a spell right after being unstunned, from the server's point of view it looks like you moved while casting. So yeah until it's fixed we have to wait a second or two before casting after stuns. This also applies to auto-attack sometimes trying to fire a Ranged shot after being stunned too, because the server thinks the client is in a different location that is out of melee range.

replies.author: Kreigr
replies.text: TY for the added info.

1542932313053331606.title: Potential Bug – Offensive Stance may not activate correctly after login
1542932313053331606.report:
I believe I may have found an issue with Warrior Offensive Stance. I normally leave Offensive Stance active at all times, and after logging in the UI continues to show it as active.

I noticed that my melee performance seemed significantly worse than expected, including an unusually high number of misses even against mobs several levels below me with capped weapon skill.

I then switched Offensive → Striker → Offensive, and combat performance noticeably improved.

I've since done some pre- and post-toggle parsing/analysis, and the data is leaning toward this being an actual bug rather than just RNG.

My current theory is that Offensive Stance visually persists as active after login, but its underlying bonuses may not always be applied until the player switches stances and reactivates Offensive.

I'm continuing to test it, but wanted to report it and see if anyone else can reproduce the behavior. If you're a Warrior who stays in Offensive, try comparing a fresh-login parse before touching your stance against one after toggling to another stance and back to Offensive.

1541246055213965353.title: DD Spells in combat log don't always reflect their upgraded status.
1541246055213965353.report:
Wish I could just post a screenshot, but here's a quick attempt at explaining what the combat log is showing for upgraded DD spells...

When you cast a spell, it shows up like this:

You begin casting Scorching Arrow VI - with a link that shows the properly upgraded spell. If the spell lands, the next message is:

You hit %t for 252 points of fire damage by Scorching Arrow - with a link to the BASE spell info, even though 252 is the proper dmg for rank VI. Oddly, if it gets resisted you get this message instead:

%t resisted your Scorching Arrow VI - with a link the the properly upgraded spell. 

This makes it look at a glance like sometimes it casts the upgraded spell (and gets resisted) and other times it casts the base spell and lands, but it's really always casting the upgraded spell.

To make it further confusing, DOTs don't seem to have that problem. The DOT portion of that same Scorching Arrow spell? It comes across like:

%t has taken 126 damage from your Scorching Arrow VI - with a link to the properly upgraded spell.

So far I have seen that all of my DD spells and DD procs work exactly like this. Call of Sky, Vampiric Embrace, and the BST warder proc buffs. Doesn't matter if it's instant cast proc or a casted nuke, the behavior is the same.

replies.author: SeppTB
replies.text: Factions in this era have what are called reaction modifiers, These are modifiers based on race, class, and diety that adjust the possible range of factions. It means certain combos will not be capable of getting all the way to ally, and in some cases, never even able to get above scowling. Specifically for Kerra Isle faction, Troll has -1000, Cazic Thule has -1000, and if you have necro or SK in your list, you have another -1000 or -2000 if both. That'd push you to where you cannot get above scowling. Later expansions abandoned this system, but classic has them for almost every single faction.

replies.author: SeppTB

1541119922082676856.title: Rogue utility poison buffs often block each other instead of overwriting
1541119922082676856.report:
Certain utility poisons, specifically the self buffs applied to the rogue, freely overwrite each other. This seems like the desired effect, still enforcing the 1 utility poison at a time restriction, while allowing them to be swapped out as the situation demands.

Many other utility poisons arbitrarily block each other, which seems unintentional and makes it confusing to figure out what swaps are "legal". The only way to circumvent this is to manually click-off the current poison from the buff window when applying a new poison.

Generally, the basic poisons (applying 1 debuff) overwrite each other, except for Clumsiness which blocks all others. The combo poisons (applying 2 debuffs) start making the combinatorics tricky. Here's what I've tested, up to Level 30:

BASICS:
Banishing blocks: Binding, Fettering, Mind Wrack, Neurotoxin
Befuddling blocks: Binding, Mind Wrack, Neurotoxin
Clumsiness blocks: Banishing, Befuddling, Binding, Concussive, Fettering, Grounding, Hobbling, Mind Wrack, Neurotoxin, Weakening
Concussive blocks: Binding
Grounding blocks: Binding, Mind Wrack, Neurotoxin
Hobbling blocks: Binding, Mind Wrack, Neurotoxin
Weakening blocks: none

COMBOS:
Binding blocks: none
Fettering blocks: Befuddling, Binding, Concussive, Hobbling, Mind Wrack, Neurotoxic, Weakening
Mind Wrack blocks: Binding, Weakening
Neurotoxic blocks: Binding, Concussive, Mind Wrack, Weakening

(Not tested: Thought Drain, Antimagic, Mage Bane, Paralytic)

replies.author: Severd8
replies.text: Same issue here.

replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: If you get a skill up report but the number doesn’t change like shown in the screenshot, that’s a known cosmetic bug with any skill increase AA. It happens with the tradeskill one too. Logging out to character select and logging back in will fix it and display the correct number going forward. (Occasionally zoning will too, but I recommend a relog.) Trendari, are you getting skill increase reports with no number change like Visadrix’s screenshot? Or are you not seeing any skill increase reports at all? If you’re not see any skill hit reports at all, log out and in, but DO NOT change loadouts. The additional specialization AA bugs out when you swap loadouts. Double check the skill window. (Inventory, skill button.) Scroll down to the specializations. The capped specs should be capped at 50. The uncapped ones should report X / Y. What are you seeing? It should be the original and evocation. Here’s the extra bad news. This has a ton of reports. As I mentioned, swapping loadouts bug the AA and will change the specialization points in alphabetical order. Meaning if you have two over 50, a loadout swap will set you to Alteration and Abjuration as your specialties. If you’ve swapped loadouts already and you’re set to alteration and abjuration, the only way to get evocation is buy the AA again, skill up, and not swap loadouts. The semi good news regarding the bug is that you can buy all the specialization AA and be able to get all of the spell skills over the cap of 50.

>Since I am not editing any loadout that is not currently loaded, I am not copying Current UI or Equip.

replies.author: StOo
replies.text: Pathing in PoS is completely b0rked. About 10% of the time if you pull a flying mob they will just go "MY PEOPLE NEED ME!" and disappear into the wild blue yonder, aggroing mobs on other islands. I don't know how EQ pathing works under the hood, but from observation it looks a very basic node graph system. *The following is total speculation on my part*: Z-axis may be disregarded when selecting nodes, so although a node above/below a mob might be a closer beeline, only X and Y are considered when doing distance checks so flying mobs can sometimes select a node on another island.

replies.author: Jukeboxx
replies.text: That combined with the fact that mobs will warp to their target if they can't find a viable path, and then once they are damaged they also can summon you over level 50 (inconsistent which ones do and don't summon after kunark) all these systems were because the pathing system so bad they put these workaround in so people would stop abusing pathing/geometry to kill things without risk. They eventually abandoned the summoning mechanic. I even remember a raid in Underfoot where you kite the final boss the whole time. 1540023074005590056.title: Berserker Blood Rune capped at 10 points of absorption
1540023074005590056.report:
From my testing, Blood Rune absorbs a maximum of 10 points of damage, even if the combat text indicates that a larger rune was applied.

Attaching a demo video showing the easiest repro steps I could think of, plus the logs. Here's how I tested:

1) As a 21 Enc/Wiz/Ber, I obtained AA Blood Rune rank 3, "Melee and ability critical hits give you 15% of the damage done as an absorption shield, up to 10% of your maximum hitpoints."
2) Unequip everything except for a strong 2H weapon (Cudgel of the Fool)
3) Remove all buffs
4) Assume the Offensive stance and Over Channel invocation
5) Auto-attack a level 1 mob
6) Continue until a crit happens with an applied Blood Rune > 10 points
7) Target self and cast level 0 Shock of Fire, which normally does 20 points of damage
8) Observe that 10 points of damage are dealt, showing 10 points were absorbed by the rune
9) Continue casting Shock of Fire on self, observing all subsequent casts do 20 points of damage

I repeated the test as a 10 Mag/Enc/Ber (second part of the video), using a different spell (Burn, does 14 damage), and observed the same results. I did additional testing on tougher mobs (where the mob isn't killed in 1 hit) and using stronger spells, and always observed the same thing: the rune only absorbs 10 points of damage.

1539677540065484900.title: Spellblade Invocation doesnt proc spells like Lifetap if the bard is using a song such as Solon's BB

replies.author: colexian
replies.text: Technically spellblade isn't a proc at all, it triggers a free cast on hit. You still cast the spell as normal. It still takes mana. It scales off focuses. Procs can still trigger on the same hit (normally each hit can only proc one proc per hit) Calling it a proc is just short hand. Its a pain in the butt with bard, but trust you don't want it to actually be a proc, it would go from bad to worse without focuses and eating other procs.

1539215101037383700.title: Bard Chant of Battle stacking issues
1539215101037383700.report:
Chant of Battle is one of the first songs bards get at level 1. It's a very solid buff song with no direct upgrade later on. It's the only bard song that I'm aware of that increases both strength and dex. At level 46 and rank III, I get the following stat increases from it:
-38 strength and dexterity
-9 AC 

So all in all, it's a pretty solid buff song that you never stop wanting to use. The problem with it is that there are a ton of songs you get later that don't stack with it, and I'm not really sure why. This starts almost right away with Anthem de Arms which is the first group haste song bards get at level 10. At that point, you have to choose whether you want to give your group str/dex/ac or str/haste. AC is super important, and so is haste and dex is very useful too, so having to choose either/or here kind of sucks. 

That's just the start of the stacking issues with Chant of Battle though. There are a couple other songs that you cannot run with it. Here's a list of songs I know it won't stack with, those songs effects and their spell level and which song takes priority:
-Anthem de Arms - str/haste buff - level 10 - Chant of Battle takes priority
-McVaxius' Berserker Crescendo - str/haste/ac buff - level 42 - McVaxius' takes priority
-Jonthan's Provocation - self only str/haste/attack buff - level 45 -Chant of Battle takes priority

So we see Chant of Battle has a strength buff and so do all 3 of the songs that won't stack with it, so that's where the conflict lies, right? Wrong. Here's two songs that disprove that theory:
-Jonthan's Whistling Warsong - self only str/haste/ac buff - level 7 -stacks with Chant of Battle
-Verses of Victory - str/haste/agility buff - level 50 - stacks with Chant of Battle

There are two songs with strength components that stack with CoB no problem, so that would indicate the str buff part isn't the conflict. Please fix this because you shouldn't have to decide between your best stat buff song and haste for the group.

replies.author: Osprey39
replies.text: Just to further illustrate stacking issues that are going on, Jonthan's Whistling Warsong and Jonthan's Provocation stack no problem, including the strength component. They probably shouldn't as the latter is clearly an upgrade to the former, but they do and again, Whistling Warsong will stack with Chant of Battle, but Provocation will not. It's maddening because it seems almost arbitrary.

replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: Bard song stacking is downright bizarre, I agree. I once saw a long flowchart on how to get things to stack, because by default some songs won't stack, but with effort, you can get them to stack.

replies.author: Chuggy
replies.text: First they should fix bard song upgrades before they start diving into stacking. Upgrading this spell will only raise duration and lower mana cost and cast time, value wont get raised.

replies.author: Osprey39
replies.text: Yeah, the way bard songs upgrade is kind of pointless in a world with Symphonic Aura, but that's a separate topic that should probably go in <#1483591812558880789> Let's please try to keep this thread on message so maybe it gets fixed.

replies.author: Viskar
replies.text: Bard song stacking is very obtuse, but you can stack it with Verses of Victory + Katta + Chant of Battle (for big STR/agi/Dex/AC). Or run double Jonthan's for STR/Atk. It's kind of odd but there's separate "routes" for combining songs is how I've come to understand how they pair up.

replies.author: Osprey39
replies.text: You're exactly right and what you said is illustrative of my point that there's more than likely some kind of bug at work here. If it's by design, that design needs to be changed because you shouldn't have to wait until level 45+ to get a group haste song that will stack with your primary stat buff song.

replies.author: Chuggy
replies.text: I made some postings in feedback since beta, no response so far. I hope more will realize how bad the upgrade situation is for buffs and songs is and will help to get the devs attention on this

replies.author: Osprey39
replies.text: My first reaction after reading your post was to make a really snarky reply in return, but I took a minute and now I'm ready to have an intelligent conversation. To answer your accusation, I mained a bard on Quarm, so it wasn't even that long ago, but I vaguely remember the issue with Anthem de Arms and Chant of Battle not stacking. To be honest though, I soloed most of the time on my bard so I was usually running Jonthan's and didn't encounter this issue much. I also will admit that remembering something like that isn't real high on my priority list As for it being that way for 25 years, can you think of anything that they have changed for Legends from how the game worked for 25 years? I can think of one thing with bards that absolutely doesn't work like it did 25 years ago. Your AE damage songs only hit stuff on your hate list in Legends instead of anything that's in range of you. That was absolutely not the case in classic EQ. If that (among many other custom changes) can be done, I see no reason why this can't be, because it makes no damn sense. Allow me to elaborate by using your statement: "the song conflicts by providing by some of the same stat components, of songs you want to stack it with," The thing is, I spelled that out in the original post that the only common denominator in the stuff it doesn't stack with is strength, but yet the songs it does stack with also have a strength component, so there is no logic to what stacks and what doesn't. That's why I said in the OP that it seems arbitrary, because there is no rhyme nor reason to it.

1539101927684444251.title: Plane of Fear Issue Causing False Anit-Cheat Flags
1539101927684444251.report: I spent a good part of the day in PoF in a eight man raid. We cleared all side bosses and CT in D0 through D4, including the fear bombing dragonlich boss. Lost connection only once during the time there. After we were through ported out via Origin then the game froze up. I waited around five or so min to clear normally. Afterwards, after it seemd it would not clear up. I went into Ctl+Alt+Del and force cloesed the game. Attempted to log back in and got a message that the account was temp blocked from entering the server. please try again (see attached). Thinking this was an error in the lancher, I uninstalled and reinstalled the game with no change. Reaching out to support, I was told that my account was on 24 hour blocked for cheating by the automtic anti-cheat system. Did some research and found that this has happened to others in Plane of Fear due to issues with character tracking when feared triggering the system into thinking that there is a speed hack or some type of teleporting cheat being used. After emailing support, they removed the block and was instructed to report the glitch/bug here for further review.

1539055567086293153.title: Proc rates seem rather low
1539055567086293153.report:
Burn proc exaltation from Smoldering Brand, which doesn't show any modifier to proc rate, with 334 dex proced 9 times across 10 minutes of straight combat time across several Eye of Veeshan fights only casting frost shard between swings

During that same timeframe pet's mainhand exaltation proc, Soul Leech which also doesn't show a modifier, proc'd 26 times across the same 10 minute at 417 dex stretch, which still feels rather low for 417 dex, but not as bad as the above.

Comparatively, Spirit of Vermin proc has a 150% mod and proc'd 53 times over 10 minutes (and resisted 47, but that's a different post). Ballpark math this is around 5ppm, removing for the 1.5mod means a ~3.3ppm rate is what 417 dex gives, which could be accurate even if it seems low for that dex.. But if so that means weapon-based procs are firing quite a way less than they should.

I know procs are fuzzy but I was under the impression that ppm for most effects is at least 1 if not 2ppm, depending on era/server/timeline/etc. My ppm is barely 1 per minute and pet is at 2.5ish (and 5 for 1.5mod) but that's at >400 dex. Was base proc lowered due to high stat caps, if so isn't that kinda misleading? 

We really need some feedback. EQ has so many iterations and mechanics that it's near impossible to tell what's intended or not. It's creating a lot of friction when the entire underlying point of the server is theorycrafting and mixing and matching classes and exaltations and AAs and things in creative ways. Most may not notice now but they'll notice when grinding and staying sub'd for the weekly motes and that extra +1 doesn't *do* anything, then quit. Why farm/grind a proc exalt if it adds <1 dps?

I can't decide if any item upgrade is worth motes or what gear to farm and chase if nothing works the way it's supposed and everyone assumes it's just like EQ. So it begs the question: are the mechanics supposed to work like EQ or are they not? Have they been altered substantially?

replies.author: Alebrije
replies.text: Lifetap strike proc, from Boon of the Garou, interestingly proc'd for me during that same 10 minute window 48 times - which would actually align a lot more closely with a proc rate I'd expect at >300dex, spell-based procs seem to be firing off way more (or just normally?)

replies.author: ThisGuyOverHere

replies.author: Shivan_Angel
replies.text: That is really odd. I actually tested procs last night wondering if the were firing like they should be. It was incredibly consistent across multiple parses, not matter how many procs I added, 1,2,3 up to 7 they would all have the same number of procs over 20 minutes within a 1-2 total variance for each individual proc. So for example Proc 1 would proc 40 times Add proc 2 Proc 1 41 times, proc 2 22 times Add proc 3, Proc 1 42 times, Proc 2 22 times, Proc 3 22 times. Etc all the way up to 7. I tested this at 185 dec. I am wondering, cause I have heard this procs being broken and have seen similar data, if dex over a certain threshold is lowering proc chance for whatever reason, or something similar. I dont have the ability on the character im testing on to push my dex higher yet, but I kind of want to do some more testing with high dex.

replies.author: Shivan_Angel
replies.text: So PPM formula is Dex/170+0.5 which I have found accurate on EQL in my testing. So at 334 dex you should have 2.5ppm essentially. So the brand is significantly under that which is odd. The pet at 417 dex, should be at 2.95 ppm which is pretty close considering 10 minutes of parsing and the variance of a short parse.

replies.author: Shivan_Angel
replies.text: Just did a 56 minute parse because I was curious. I have 215 dex so that puts me at 1.76ppm I was DWing so 1.76 ppm mainhand, 0.88ppm offhand for a total of 2.64 ppm Dual ignite procs, 140 total procs. or 2.5ppm which is close to 2.64 especially with a low ppm and only a 56 minute parse. Asp Venom 165 procs, or 2.94pm, slightly higher but still within the realm of 2.64 Vamp embrace, 167 procs or 2.98 ppm sstill within the realm of 2.64. Unless there is something odd with that particular proc, this all suggests that procs are working based on what we know. a 10 minute parse, with a 2.5 ppm in your scenario, can lead to a high amount of variability. Also wondering how many total swings with the weapon in your mainhand over that 10 minutes. If the proc is only in your mainhand. This is not saying with 100% certainty that something isnt wrong in your scenario, but I think with numbers as low as 2.5ppm, that a longer parse might be warranted to narrow variance. Other people have reported that proc chance feels low or have posted similar parses to yours showing a low ppm so very well could be something to it, they also all had fairly high dex, so leads me to wonder if something is going on, is it related to dex over the cap in classic EQ and something is making it act up. Would need someone with significantly higher dex then me to test it. My brother is a sham and I do have a chanter as well. Maybe when he calls it a night ill have him dex buff me, throw on a garou and see what a repeat parse with around 360 dex looks like.

replies.author: Razel the Rogue
replies.text: I was planning a deeper breakdown for later for my Rogue 101 guides, but here is my understanding. Firstly, I think your insight is spot on. Here is my understanding of how Strength, Attack, and AC interact: * Attack: Dictates how heavily a mob’s damage rolls skew toward its maximum hit. * Strength Debuffs: Lowering a mob’s STR directly reduces its Attack, shifting damage rolls away from top-end hits. * Armor Class (AC): High-AC classes (WAR, PAL, SK) naturally push damage distributions down toward a mob's minimum hit. ## High Max Damage vs. Low Max Damage Mobs (Note: These are illustrative napkin numbers to demonstrate the concept.) ## Compare a high-STR, high-max-damage mob like Nagafen (e.g., 350 max hit) with a lower-max-damage mob like Yael (e.g., 150 max hit). ### High Max Hit (Nagafen) Baseline: High base Attack skews damage rolls heavily toward the 350 cap. Low-AC targets get hit for 300+ almost every swing. With STR Debuffs: Dropping Attack flattens the distribution. Against a low-AC character, damage rolls shift from a tight 325–350 range down toward 275–300, creating a drastic reduction in incoming DPS. High-AC Impact: High-AC tanks already force lower damage rolls, so the STR debuff provides a much smaller difference. ### Low Max Hit (Yael) Baseline: With lower base Attack and a lower damage cap, Yael rarely hits peak numbers to begin with. With STR Debuffs: Reducing STR slightly lowers an already-infrequent top-end hit. The overall DPS change is barely noticeable for either high- or low-AC targets. Again those numbers are not the real numbers. My parses showed Naggy hitting me for about 170 avg and Yael 110 avg. ### Summary I will redo the tests at a later date--I am enjoying the game for now. That is my understanding, though I certainly don't claim to be an expert—I'm still learning/re-learning mechanics ~30 years into this game. ### TLDR; Debuffs work, but the affects are relative to Mob dmg range, attack, and your AC.

1538367220818649098.title: Certain NPC debuffs acting like cancel magic
1538367220818649098.report:
Quick mechanics question: are mob DoTs/snares/debuffs supposed to overwrite beneficial buffs?

I’ve noticed a few cases where a hostile spell lands and a beneficial buff drops at the same time.

Spirit of BihLi vs Dooming Darkness:

[Fri Aug 14 14:08:12 2026] A heart harpie begins casting Dooming Darkness.
[Fri Aug 14 14:08:14 2026] The spirit of BihLi leaves you.
[Fri Aug 14 14:08:14 2026] You are engulfed by darkness.

Divine Purpose vs Chilling Embrace:

[Fri Aug 14 11:17:28 2026] An ashenbone drake begins casting Chilling Embrace.
[Fri Aug 14 11:17:31 2026] The divine flame leaves.
[Fri Aug 14 11:17:31 2026] You are wracked by chilling poison.

Rage vs Insidious Retrogression:

[Sat Aug 15 21:50:51 2026] Lady Vox begins casting Insidious Retrogression.
[Sat Aug 15 21:50:53 2026] Your frenzy fades.
[Sat Aug 15 21:50:53 2026] Lady Vox hit you for 532 points of disease damage by Insidious Retrogression.

I checked the local spell data for Insidious Retrogression and it looks like disease damage + snare/STR/ATK debuff, not an explicit dispel/cancel magic effect.

Is this intended spell-line/slot overwrite behavior, or does it look like hostile debuffs/DoTs are incorrectly knocking off beneficial buffs?

I have had people tell me that this is how it behaved in 99. However, in 99 people weren't fighting multi class mobs so their chance of encountering a mob that would remove these buffs was significantly less. 

Its extremely annoying to have to reapply buffs after almost every fight. 

 or could you please take this to the dev team

replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: It's a bit counter intuitive, but there's a reason for the display. It's kinda complicated, so bear with me. (But the TLDR is that it works that way to keep it simple.) Faction is a value on a scale of -2000 to +2000. It's tied to your character and represents the actions you've taken. Everyone starts at 0. Everyone has a minimum of -2000. Everyone has a max of +2000. But then we have modifiers. The UI displays the *current* point total. It doesn't display modifiers. Just the total. The math is done behind the screen. Let's say +10 race -50 class modifier +60 deity modifier = +20. (Values pulled from the ether), then it shows the final result: Indifferent (+20). To be helpful, it tells you how many points to the next level descriptor. Using my example: 80 points to Amiably. But again, it's only looking at the current total of the invisible math. The value of the final result is then compared to the descriptor scale and gives you the tooltip. It would be nice if it showed you the modifiers, but I'm guessing the EQ UI devs decided simpler is better. I think the counter intuitive part is the modifiers. Modifiers move the needle and change the value. But the modifiers aren't fixed. Both here and on live, you can change your race, class, and deity in various ways. And there are other modifiers like the faction song and faction spells. Or in some cases, things like sneak will set your faction to a specific level. Sneak always sets you to indifferent, for example. Knowing how close you are helps to determine what other tools you need. But the modifiers are never really explained. Thanks to the lack of transparency of the modifiers, it provides counter intuitive expectations of the UI and the community members will deliver the modified value as if it were the absolute value, and it's not. As a side note, I'm guessing your comp had druid, monk, and/or ranger. That gives you +10 on top of the Iksar -1000 and Cazic -300 for the guards.

replies.text: I dont understand why there is confusion on this topic. Have you guys not all gotten the barons blade and upgraded it? It starts with 10 damage. My hypothesis is it needs a single point of exp to bump up to its upgrade but thats easier said than done. So finding 1 extra sword has always done it for weapons that break at 6. Like all weapons i have leveled that are due an upgrade at +6. Each level represents a 10% increase to the base damage. For the befallen 2 swords, 20 dmg ending at +10 and a 100% increase to the base damage. Theres no x of 1024 math involved. Its level by level. Otherwise why would leveling from 0 to +1 raise weapon damage from 10 to 11 when the sword is at 1/1024??? So its pretty easy to see each upgrade is meant to be a 10% increase. For weapons that are below 10 that means they do not receive an upgrade every level on the level but often between level ups.

1537267007349723248.title: Pet Weapon Equipping Bugs
1537267007349723248.report:
There are a few bugs currently with how and when pets choose to wield weapons. 

The first and arguably most important bug is related to the damage bonus granted to the pets by leveling spells. This bug has two parts. The first part is that weapon damage is applied solely to the pet if it is not wielding a weapon. It is not applied when wielding a weapon.

The second part is related to the first part; the bonus damage is added before the ratio comparison to see if the pet should use the weapon. This happens because the damage is added to the pets base. Really the comparison between the two objects should happen before the damage bonus is applied, then the bonus should be applied. 

The second bug is related to how pets choose to wield weapons. When a pet is making the decision whether to wield a weapon or not, if the weapon's base damage is higher, but the ratio is not, the pet will still choose to wield that weapon. This can cause a DPS loss if the pet uses a weapon with a worse ratio than their base ratio.

The third bug is related to the second bug. In specific cases where the ratio is lower, but the base damage is higher, the pet will instead choose to use its base delay with the weapon. This seems to happen if the weapon is sufficiently slow (any weapon over 50 delay I’ve tested seems to do this, including earthshaker and gardash). Also in this case the pet will use its base damage bonus rather than the weapons damage bonus.

1536853125011607592.title: Pet Illusion Selection Does Not Recognize +2 or Higher Items in Activated Items Storage
1536853125011607592.report:
There appears to be an issue with illusion items stored in Storage → Activated Items when attempting to use them through the Pet Illusion slot.

Items with an illusion click effect work correctly from Activated Items Storage at base/+0 and +1, but once the item is upgraded to +2 or higher, the illusion no longer appears/functions as an available Pet Illusion.

Examples:
• Amulet of Necropotence +0/+1 → Skeleton illusion works as a Pet Illusion.
• Amulet of Necropotence +2 or higher → Does not work as a Pet Illusion.
• Guise of the Deceiver +0/+1 → Works as a Pet Illusion.
• Guise of the Deceiver +2 or higher → Does not work as a Pet Illusion.

The upgraded items themselves still function correctly from Activated Items Storage. I can click/activate their effects normally on my character. The issue appears to be specifically with the Pet Illusion system recognizing the upgraded item.

I've tested this with multiple illusion items and have been able to reproduce the behavior.

Possible cause:
+2 is also the point where an item's click effect becomes eligible to be extracted. My guess is that once the item becomes eligible for effect extraction, the Pet Illusion system may no longer recognize the illusion effect on the original item. *This is only a theory based on the consistent +2 breakpoint.*

Expected behavior:
If an illusion item is stored in Activated Items Storage, its illusion should remain available through the Pet Illusion slot regardless of whether the item is +0, +1, +2, +3, +4, etc., just as the item's normal click effect remains usable.

- Loadout 1 has an FBSS equipped.

- I switch to Loadout 2, which still has the FBSS saved as its belt.
- The upgraded belt from Loadout 1 is no longer available to equip or assign to Loadout 2 because it is tied up in Loadout 1's equipment set.

1536185033914847433.title: Rogue Poisons Apply Magic Counters Instead of Poison Counters
1536185033914847433.report: Rogue poisons can be dispelled via magic dispels like Pillage Enchantment and Banishing Strike, which explicitly dispel magic effect.

replies.author: Avatarded
replies.text: All poisons can be dispelled in that way. Yes, even poisons used on you by enemies.

replies.author: jeditobe1
replies.text: Diseases (ex slows) and poisons (ex tash) which have counters definitely cannot be dispelled that way. The rogue poisons need counters if they are to require poison curing. The flipside of that is that the cure spells can't target enemies (I believe), so once poisoned with a spell with poison counters, you can't really remove it of for example you want to mez something.

replies.author: Sotsu
replies.text: This is incorrect. Magic effects, positive or negative are dispellable with magic dispels. The way dispels work are by removing counters, each buff/debuff are applied with a preset number of counters and each dispel removes a preset number of those counters. This is why you have upgraded versions of dispels, they remove more counters. These counters are specific to the school (magic, disease, curse, poison), and each dispel removes counters specific to their dispel schools. My argument here is that rogues have poisons, but their poisons are applying magic counters instead of poison counters. They should be dispelled via poison dispel, not magic dispel.

replies.author: jeditobe1
replies.text: Disease/curse/poison have counters, I dont think there are counters on magic effects (even hidden ones). Instead, dispells work on a chance based system, and target effects that are tagged as dispellable/curable without any counters.

replies.text: AARRGGHH.... I _finally_ solved this! The spare PC is the one I operate with my left hand. Thus it's set up with the mouse (well, trackball) set to "Left Handed" mode. 1534994600626884830.title: I'm sure this has been posted somewhere but not finding the post, or I'm too lazy.
1534994600626884830.report:
So a level 5 mote when put into a spell will give you 16 experience, which is the same for every mote based on level.

A level 5 mote on a weapon/armor piece it will give you 5. So to upgrade a +4 item to +5, one level 5 mote will give you five points. So you would need 4 level 5 motes, which would come to 20 because it requires 16 to upgrade, and then have 3 level over for the next level.

So now that the item is level 5, it will only take a level 6 mote. To create a level 6 mote you need two level 5 motes, which before would have given 10xp to an item, now the level 6 mote gives you 6, so even at level 5 you are losing 4xp per mote.

Someone need a refresher on how maths works?

replies.author: Mat
replies.text: Motes are bad for items good for spells after +4 They count for essentially the numerical value of the rank they are when used on items but will move a spell a whole level of their appropriate rank.

replies.author: Memnoch
replies.text: Correct. So they're basically making the only logical way to upgrade any weapon/armor to the three void motes you get a week then.

replies.author: Porygon
replies.text: Thats what they want, they have repeatedly stated (in response to similar threads like this) that they want the primary way of upgrading gear to be farming another piece, and combining them together.

1534599951177486426.title: Ranger's Level 50 Permanent Buff 'Force of Nature' tons of Buff Stacking issues
1534599951177486426.report:
I was looking forward to the level 50 ranger buff "Force of Nature" until I got to start using it, sadly it is nearly unusable because of a list of my own personal buffs and debuffs enemies cast on me removing it constantly.

Buffs that I know that overwrites/blocks it:
- Shaman's 'Chloroplast' Overwrites Force of Nature and vise vers
- Kilva's Skin of Flame DS Potion
- Enemy snares such as Necro/SK Darkness Line
- Enchanter's Boon of Garou
- Enemy ranger/druid snares
- SK/Necro's Heat Blood 
The buff falls off so often I can never pin down which buff/debuff is overwriting it

replies.author: Korveinous
replies.text: Doesn't stack with Boon of Garou either which I fail to see the overlap on

replies.author: Scouser
replies.text: Add Heat Blood to that list

replies.author: Maleix
replies.text: Added both, thanks

replies.author: Injuric
replies.text: I've resorted to using Nature's Precision instead of Force of Nature, at least that never seems to get overwritten. So annoying. Wolf form is equally annoying with any snare.

replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: Let’s start with some spell data to compare: Force of nature 1 : Increase ATK by 20 2 : Increase Damage Shield by 5 3 : Increase Hitpoints by 6 per tick. Max: 19 per tick 4 : Increase Endurance by 6 per tick. Max: 19 per tick Kilva’s Shield of flame 2 : Increase Damage Shield by 1 (L1) to 31 (L60) Boon of the Garou 1 : Illusion: 14 2 : Add Proc: LifetapEffectNormal 3 : Increase ATK by 30 4 : Increase DEX by 100 Let’s go through the stacking conflicts: Slot 2 damage shield in FoN and Kilva’s. That prevents stacking by design. Not a bug unless dev meant to assign the DS portion to another slot. Both FoN and Boon have atk buffs, but in completely different spell slots. They should stack. Definitely a bug. FoN doesn’t have a movement effect, so druid/ranger snares shouldn’t affect it. Also definitely a bug. Dots? Inclusive of the darkness line, ranger fast cast nuke/dot, heat blood, and others: Currently dots are stripping anything with a regen effect. (Including but not limited to Iksar and bear illusion, chloro, regen, mage armor line.) There’s a ton of bug reports on it. I’ve responded to at least 10 of them and more keep popping up. Is this a bug? No idea. It is a known issue based on the bajillion reports during POB and now, but dev hasn’t publicly commented that I’m aware of.

replies.author: nirafelos
replies.text: I certainly hope they treat it as a bug. the multiclassing mobs in higher difficulties make caster mobs exponentially more common, and render all of those regen spells pretty fully unusable unless you want to dedicate a permanent slot on your spell bar, mana, and time to recast them every third pull. With all of the quality of life upgrades this server brings, this issue feels like an anomalous instance of really bad QoL sneaking in. If we didn’t have those QoL upgrades elsewhere, I’d probably be in the camp of “yeah EQ spell stacking was janky, isn’t it charming?” — but we do, so it instead feels wholly inconsistent with the design philosophy.

replies.author: Kel
replies.text: There are some weird stacking bugs happening with Force of Nature, Wolf Form. and Nature's Precision. If you cast Wolf Form first, then Force of Nature, it says Force was blocked by wolf form. HOWEVER, if you cast WF and NP first, THEN Force, it will only overwrite NP and you have both WF and Force active simulataneously.

replies.author: Roffles / Ermahgerdden
replies.text: force of nature gets overwritten by so many things...I don't even bother with it on my spell bar anymore even though its really good.

replies.author: oSlash
replies.text: Has this improved after the last patch? So many buffs that used to get knocked off before don't anymore (looking at you rage and the million necros out there)

replies.author: Ayomi
replies.text: Yes, it has improved. FoN does get overwritten by Chloroplast, which is annoying, but beyond that FoN won't get overwritten anymore. To use both Wolf Form and FoN at the same time do the following, Cast Wolf Form -> Cast Nature's Precision -> Cast Force of Nature. FoN will overwrite Nature's Precision, but leave Wolf Form up letting you benefit from both. Get permanent illusion so you don't have to recast it every time you zone. FoN also pairs well with Shaman/Beastlord as it stacks with their Frenzy/Rage line of spells. So you can have Wolf Form, FoN, Rage, Hawk Eye, Spikecoat, Call of Sky all as self permanent buffs. FoN does block the call of earth line, as expected, since they both provide extra dmg shields and are of the same spell line. All other duration buffs (Excluding Chloroplast lines and Call of Earth lines) will stack with this setup as far as I know. So that means you could have all Shaman buffs and all Cleric/Paladin buffs up in addition to the above setup.

1534323357019934760.report: When i try to move my move my Short sword of Ykesha Exaltation from my +8 Barons blade into my +4 Flaming fists it says "the result of this comb will produce an unusable item" is that by design or bug ? Same thing with Ruby Stiletto Exaltation

replies.author: Enorfir
replies.text: Yes, the Flaming Fist and Short Sword of the Ykesha don't share any classes in their restrictions, so if you were to combine them no one would be able to use it

replies.author: 𝐃𝐫𝐚𝐯𝐞
replies.text: Monk/Bst have to be able to use the weapon the proc came from.

replies.author: MathSlinger
replies.text: so i'm a monk/sham/bard combo

replies.author: 𝐃𝐫𝐚𝐯𝐞
replies.text: Yeah, but the fists are MNK/BST only.

replies.author: MathSlinger
replies.text: so i have to be a monk/bst for the proc to go into it?

replies.author: SeppTB
replies.text: Exalt system does not care about your classes. It's looking at the classes of the item, and the classes of the exalt, and what the resulting item will be, which is only those that overlap. MNK/BST are not on Ykesha, so it cannot go into Flaming Fist because there'd then be no classes that can use that item.

replies.author: Reidas
replies.text: no, that proc can never go into the fists, because mnk/bst aren't on the yakesha proc.

replies.author: walk2k
replies.text: it has to be a legal item

replies.author: MathSlinger
replies.text: i get it now, that makes sense, ty

replies.author: Alebrije
replies.text: It's a little restrictive with how it works from base EQ and I fear it's gonna become kinda problematic once we get into more class-specific quests/gears and tons of stuff simply can't be overlapped at all

replies.author: MathSlinger
replies.text: so it would only work if Ykehsa was usable by monk/ or bst, but since its only WAR pal, rng, shd, bard, rog it won't go into a monk/bst weapon... yes, got it, ty all

replies.author: walk2k
replies.text: also, if the proc is Primary only you can't put it on a weapon in your Secondary slot. it will tell you this if you try.. you have to move it to Primary slot (or inventory) first. and then of course that weapon can't go back in Secondary slot with that aug on it

replies.author: MathSlinger
replies.text: sweet, ty for the heads up

replies.author: Alebrije
replies.text: It will only ever be usable by the classes which overlap on both items, which means basically no criss-crossing of focus effects/procs/etc. from any archetypical items onto others

1533947598073757757.title: NPC Pet Agro Bug?
1533947598073757757.report: Based on the behavior I've observed, I need to lull a mob and the mob's pet in order to pull past it. This seems to imply that the pet is agroing independently of the pet's owner. I do not believe this is the case in live. Splitting tight rooms with many pets (like LGuk Assassin) can be impossible even with lull because of how agro chains and radiates. It pushes everything too close together - mob A is now directly next to mob B's pet, whereas the two owner mobs are far enough apart for a successful lull. And even if it's not agroing at pull, your mob has a higher chance of running directly through the orbit of a pet and agroing the pet, and then the owner, etc. I think this issue amplifies the need to have an enchanter and reduces build variety. It also requires that you lull twice as many mobs if you have a lot of pet class NPCs in a room.

1532828604533309660.title: Bard's Cantata songs don't stack with Cassindra songs
1532828604533309660.report:
My understanding is that Cantata of Soothing (level 34) should stack with Cassindra's Chorus of Clarity (level 32) or Cassindra's Chant of Clarity (level 20), ultimately improving mana regen compared to playing either song line individually. Currently, they are mutually exclusive. Cantata and Chorus overwrite each other, while Cantata completely blocks Chant. When Cantata is granted at level 34, it provides the same mana regen as Chorus (plus health and endurance), making Chorus obsolete rather than additive, which seems unintentional.

Having stacking mana regen was a big reason for putting Bard in my trio, so selfishly I hope this can be looked into!

When they changed to be buff icons stacking was different. Using P99 resources will give you info that doesn't line up with this code base very well, both because EQL started from live EQ source, and changes since

Back in 2000 I put in a ticket because the "fab four" guards in Dagnor's Cauldron would attack me if I brought an Undertow Skeleton too near their camp. The GMs didn't believe me, so six of them sat down and watched as I used my ranger to find skeletons and bring them to the camp, only to have the guards murder me. We did this quite a few times. replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: Less than you might think. I was able to fix it by starting the peace keeper's staff quest and redoing the first step. ( Get to amiable with the Peace Keepers. Your faction modifiers are erudite is +50, paladin +50, and quellious follower +100. You only need to be at +100 or better. Since everyone starts at 0, I used illusion erudite and had paladin in my loadout. That gave me +100 to pick up the quest. Talk to the NPC in Erudin to get the letter. Letter is no longer lore, so stock up on as many as you'd like. I hope you have lots of bag space. Head out to Tox. The turn in NPC is just SW of the entrance to Erudin. He's *on* the merchants of erudin faction, but he accepts the turn in at indifferent. So get behind him. Use sneak. Once sneak is successful and he becomes indifferent, turn in the letters one by one until you reach the desired rep. I was at kindly to the merchants, high council, and high guard when I was done. All you have to do at that point is to destroy all the staffs in your inventory.

replies.author: Enarei
replies.text: Sadly the first step in the quest, the note to Emil, is broken.

replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: Really? 'Cause I literally just did it.

replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: Three screenshots. The letters, my faction on turn ins, and the faction hits.

replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: And an extra screenshot for the PK staves I just picked up.

replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: Now that I actually have time, let's go through this in detail. My previous guide above assumes you are playing a default kerran, no negative faction hits with erudites except heretic and the ones Creot's death causes. Or to put it another way, it's written for agnostic kerrans who have done only the kerran quests up to this point and have had no faction hits with the Peace Keepers. If you have any other race/class/religion or you've somehow had faction hits with Peace Keepers, the guide might not work. I'm going to make this a general walkthrough for everyone. The important faction standings to complete the "Letter to Emil" step are +100 peace keepers and +0 merchants of Erudin, AFTER all modifiers. Actually, the only *important* faction standing is +100 peacekeepers after modifiers, but we'll get to that. Step 1: Pick up the letter. Quest giver is Lumi Stergnon in the Temple of Divine Light in Erudin. You need +100 peacekeeper faction. The easy way is some combination of erudite, paladin, and Quellious as your deity. If you don't follow Quellious, you should be good with any deity EXCEPT Rallos Zek. (-500 faction modifier.) Lumi is a cleric guildmaster and will show up on /find. You may need to uncheck "only show destinations I can use." Erudite is easy with illusion: erudite (enchanter 12): +50 rep. Paladin is easy with a combo swap: +50 rep. You can check your standing with /faction or EQL button, character, faction standings, and click the "Everquest" category. Do a search for "peace". The window is known to bug out, so that might not work. But... Con Lumi. He needs to be amiable or better. If you're not amiable, it won't work. If you using the sneak trick, that won't work because they set your faction to +0 regardless of modifiers. Hail Lumi. Click "new acolyte of peace". Click "Retrieve the Peacekeeper staffs." He should give you a letter for Emil Parsini. The letters aren't lore, so stock up on all the letters you want or can carry.

replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: Step 2: Deliver the letter to Emil. If you haven't taken any faction hits turn in letter. Win faction hits and some staffs. (You'll probably want to destroy the staffs.) But if you have taken some faction hits, you won't be able to turn in the letter. This is counterproductive given this is the easy way to fix negative Merchants of Erudin faction. But fun fact. A good number of quests, including this one, only have a faction requirement to pick up a step. But the turn in can be anything indifferent or better. It's why the sneak trick works for so many quest turn ins. Sneak sets your faction to +0, with no applied modifiers for the duration of the turn in(s). At this point you need some form of sneak. Swap a class for rogue. Or if you have one high enough a bard (17), monk (8), or ranger (10) swap will work. Alternately, if you're halfling or kerran, you have it innately. Put it on your hotbar. So back to Emil. Emil will probably hate you if you've killed some good Erudites. We don't care. Get behind him. Use sneak. Con him. Is he indifferent? No? Sneak again. Repeat as necessary. Once he cons indifferent from sneak, turn in the letters. Win faction hits and some staffs. (You'll probably want to destroy the staffs.)

replies.text: Having said all that. , what is your class, race, and religion combo? What is your faction standing for Peace Keepers?

replies.text: Items have different damage increase setpoints. Adding +1 doesn't necessarily add a damage per rank, it may come at level 6.2, 6.7 etc.

replies.text: Yes I understand the basics at play here. Mathematically the shimmering ruby stiletto is the perfect simple math version. It has 10 base damage. Each upgrade on any weapon adds 10% nominally. You can probably see where this is going from there but at each level up it should add one to weapons with base 10. Clearly there's a rounding error at play in the behind the scenes math

replies.author: Nixilus
replies.text: or to say it another way: Shim Rub Stil +0 is 10 dmg, +10 is 20 dmg. Each level, on the level, should give 1 additional dmg. No sooner, no later.

replies.author: Mattrick_
replies.text: What you arent understanding is that the increases do not come cleanly with each + level upgrade, sometimes the damage increase comes a bit before it or a bit after it. More often that not youre getting upgrades in large chunks and just bypassing the thresholds or only notice it when it ranks up. Its not always that “clean” for every weapon

replies.author: Nixilus
replies.text: In general yes but it should be for weapons that are 10 dmg. 10% of 10 is 1.

replies.author: Nixilus
replies.text: and every upgrade prior to this upgraded on the level

replies.text: : Nixilus is exactly right about the math. For a weapon that has 10 base damage, +1 merge level === +1 damage on the item card

1532434952119914737.title: FIXED: Crash Before Character Select / After Server Select -- #630 crash
1532434952119914737.report:
## EQL crashing after server select? Try this fix

If you choose a server in EverQuest Legends, the game starts loading, and then crashes before character select, this workaround may help.

You may also see:
- Fatal error occurred in mainthread! (Release Client #630)
- Sound Manager loaded near the end of Logs\dbg.txt
- EQL loads with Sound=0, but has no game audio

You do not need to diagnose the logs or edit Windows manually. The tool checks your PC first and stops safely if it does not match the supported setup.

### What is happening?

On affected PCs, EQL crashes while Windows is initializing Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth during startup.

RC6 temporarily hides only that MIDI component while EQL starts. Once character select begins loading, it restores the exact original Windows setting and verifies that all MIDI outputs returned.

It does not patch EQL, install drivers, change default audio devices, stop audio services, or reconfigure virtual-audio software.

### How to use it

1. Download the RC6 ZIP below — not GitHub’s automatic “Source Code” ZIP.
2. Extract the entire ZIP.
3. Close EQL and the Daybreak LaunchPad.
4. Double-click Launch EQL Audio Fix.cmd.
5. Let it open the official LaunchPad, then approve UAC.
6. Return to LaunchPad and click PLAY.
7. Keep the command window open until restoration reports PASS.

If the computer loses power or the process is interrupted, run Restore Windows MIDI.cmd from the same folder.

### Download RC6

 

RC6 completed a live launch with sound enabled, passed Sound Manager loaded without #630, reached character select, and restored the exact original Windows MIDI state.

This is still a prerelease while we collect results from other affected PCs. Please report whether it worked using the field-test form linked on the release page.

replies.author: Alphablue

replies.author: Alphablue
replies.text: ### Technical note for Daybreak This appears to be an optional Windows MIDI-synth initialization failure rather than a server or authentication problem. On the affected 64-bit Windows system: - EQL launches with Sound=1. - The client reaches Sound Manager loaded. - It then crashes with Fatal error occurred in mainthread! (Release Client #630). - A preserved x64 minidump records a 0xc0000005 null read inside C:\Windows\System32\wdmaud.drv. The first symbolized path is: > CMicrosoftGSWavetableSynth::LoadDLSFile > → CWasapiRenderer::Initialize > → wdmaud.drv null read A controlled A/B test isolated Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth: - With the normal 64-bit Drivers32\midi=wdmaud.drv registration, the cold-launch crash reproduces. - Temporarily hiding only that registration removes GS Synth while leaving every other MIDI output unchanged. - EQL then passes Sound Manager loaded with Sound=1 and reaches character select. - Restoring the exact registry value restores GS Synth and all original MIDI outputs. A possible client-side fix would be to skip Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth if EQL does not require it, or safely abandon only that optional device when its DLS/WASAPI initialization fails. The client should validate returned status codes and interfaces before continuing rather than allowing an optional MIDI component to terminate the entire process. This evidence applies to this specific Sound Manager loaded → Release Client #630 sequence. It does not establish that every #630 crash has the same cause. 1532215778693353643.title: Unable to create instances in Nektulos Forest
1532215778693353643.report: tried 4 times three of them at the guard bridge Yier 3 and once at zone beginning from Commonsloands at Tier 2, just hangs game

replies.author: AboveTheChemist
replies.text: I had glitchy issues with Nektulos instances last night, on the Rivervale server. First I tried to change difficulty to D4. It 'zoned' as if it had worked and then a minute or two later a warning in large red letters on the screen said the zone would be shut down in 15 mins. Shortly thereafter I noticed that it put me in D0 difficulty, not D4. I then tried to create a personal D4 instance, but it ended up putting me in a public D1 instance. I can't remember if I tried to create the personal instance again, or if I picked a D4 public instance, but that time it seemed to work. I was pulling orcs from the orc camp just northeast of the bridge for about 20 mins. There were single orcs that would path out from the camp far enough for me to grab them. After about 20-30 mins of that (6-8 kills or so), the mobs started warping. I tagged one of the ones that had run out from the camp, and somehow every mob in the camp warped over to me. I was more than far enough away from camp to avoid social aggro, as I had had no problems with doing the same thing for the prior 30 mins. I tried again thinking it was just bad luck, but again the mobs warped. Or, perhaps it was that I saw the mob out away from camp but in reality that was just a visual glitch and the mob was actually still close enough to camp to aggro the rest. replies.author: nirafelos
replies.text: despite the OP deleting his original message, and despite this probably not technically being a bug, I do think it falls in line with the QOL changes we've seen here to consider this. Evac/gate (or even just zoning), or mezz+memblur can leave you stuck with a 9 minute snare. and no recourse other than dispelling all of your own buffs to remove it. That's very obviously how EQ worked, but with the change to remove debuffs from killed mobs _does_ beg the question: should we have this same QOL if we exit combat via another means? I don't think it'd harm anyone to allow that QOL parity.

replies.author: Amargein
replies.text: It would be a little OP if leaving combat did it. Since FD clears combat and escape if the mob was not dotted by the rogue etc. That could lead to a lot of exploits, zoning on the other hand wouldn't yield many exploits for it

replies.author: nirafelos
replies.text: I do concede that I had not considered FD or Escape for this. At the current point in the game, most debuffs are an annoyance more than they are an active danger, so I’m not sure I agree that spending a use of these abilities, all of which (except for monk fd) are on fairly decent cooldowns, solely to clear a debuff would be overpowered. I could be wrong though! When you exit combat with a mob via fd/escape, do they immediately heal to full health/mana? they do with memory blur, which is a massive mitigating factor in why I don’t believe that would be anything beyond a quality of life change. If they don’t heal to full, I agree it would be weird/awkward for monks to end up being by far the best class for dispelling themselves.
